text:
ana: follow-up from the onboarding intake RFC meeting. small focused issue: how to treat "best-effort" fingerprints in dedupe + telemetry. proposal: mark bench_job.fingerprint_confidence and change dedupe behavior.

mike: short version: if confidence=low -> no dedupe; if confidence=high -> dedupe as usual. also add `related_fingerprints` to aid human triage when collisions suspected.

raj: add that the intake adapter should attach `canonicalization_attempted:true|false` and `canonicalization_errors` (short codes) to the bench_job proto. if attempted but failed, set confidence=low.

darya: also flag `fingerprint_source` (artifact|registry|on-demand) so triage knows whether the artifact came from a canonical registry or ad-hoc upload.

ingest-bot: telemetry note: bench-runner v2 will emit `fingerprint_confidence` and `canonicalization_attempted`.

ana: decision: default dedupe behavior controlled by confidence flag. also add UX hint in intake: "If your fingerprint confidence is low, we will not dedupe; re-run with canonicalize=true to increase confidence."

mike: will update intake adapter to set `related_fingerprints` when collision heuristics trigger (e.g., same model_sha but different quant params).

raj: i have a quick question about retention: should we keep low-confidence artifacts for 7 days only? else they bloat storage.

ana: propose 14-day retention for low-confidence, 90-day for high-confidence. put a cleanup job to notify owners before deletion.

mike: lgtm. i'll attach a small migration to intake-v2 to add `fingerprint_confidence` and `canonicalization_attempted`.
__notes: short thread, util/telemetry details, retention policy
